clue.text: Root powerless to stop runs – gets spinner

indicators.note: without power means the abbreviation for power is dropped from the word
to stop something is to plug the gap in its middle, so these letters sit between the others

blocks.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run; one of the two runs
a potato is a root vegetable, which loses its P
the second run

explanation.surface: A gardener's root crop, lacking energy, holds up the runs and ends up spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root' is the potato, not the definition; minus P it becomes OTATO, which sits between two Rs, one for each run.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is a part or device that turns around an axis, so it is literally something that spins.

clue.text: Stand up to get dress, having taken coat off first

indicators.note: removing a coat strips the outside, so the outer letters of the word go

blocks.note: dress without its first and last letters
first is written 1ST, and the digit 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone told to get dressed, having just taken their coat off, digs their heels in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' looks like part of the instruction, but it is the ordinal 1ST, read as IST.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist someone is to oppose them firmly and refuse to give way, which is what standing up to them means.

clue.text: Orthodox teen maybe trained by orthodox teen

indicators.note: something trained is shaped and drilled into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the words taken as written

explanation.surface: A conventional teenager raised in the ways of another conventional teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: The same two words do both jobs: the first time they define, the second time, with 'by', they are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a wholesome, ordinary young man, so a conventional, well-behaved teenager is an example of one.

clue.text: Plant corporation ran with little investment

indicators.note: an investment is something put into something else, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: corporation is a humorous old word for a pot belly, a tum
as dye or colour runs, it bleeds
wee means small

explanation.surface: A company that grew a factory on very little capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' and 'corporation' suggest industry; corporation is an old humorous word for a big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbleweed is a plant that breaks off when dry and is rolled along by the wind across open country.

clue.text: Number one sport to initiate change in India?

indicators.note: to initiate is to begin, so this piece is placed at the start

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
number one is a nursery word for urinating

explanation.surface: A top-ranked sport sets out to reform India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' looks like a ranking but is the childish euphemism; the sport goes before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is India's currency, and change means coins or money, so its money is the rupee.

clue.text: 24 – entertaining TV show returning with Bauer essentially really old

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the show's name is read from right to left
the essence of a word is its heart, so only the central letter is used
to entertain is to host guests inside, so the other pieces go within

blocks.note: the answer to 24-down, a stake
QI is a BBC quiz show
the middle letter of Bauer

explanation.surface: The thriller 24, with Jack Bauer at its heart, now looks like a very old show.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is not the TV series but the grid entry at 24-down; Jack Bauer is that series' hero, a deliberate red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: An antique is a valuable object of great age, and as an adjective it means dating from long ago.

clue.text: A politician ring-fencing me time achieves harmony

indicators.note: a ring fence goes all the way round, so the politician's letters surround the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
a Green is a member of an environmental party
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A politician who protects personal time finds a peaceful balance.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreement is accord between people, and harmony is the same state of peaceful, shared opinion.

clue.text: Row about computers etc being on the counter

indicators.note: counter means opposite in direction, as in counterclockwise, so the letters run upwards

blocks.note: re means concerning
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: An argument over computer equipment sitting on the shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of rows or levels placed one above another, as in theatre seating.

clue.text: Lee Mack sometimes having problem with teacher

blocks.note: a question is a problem to be solved
a master is a schoolteacher

explanation.surface: The comedian Lee Mack occasionally has trouble with a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Lee Mack is a British comedian who hosts the TV quiz The 1% Club, hence a quiz host only sometimes.
explanation.definitionFit: A question master is the host who asks the questions on a quiz show, a role this comedian plays on television.

clue.text: Jumbo jet taking off first, overtaking plane travelling with husband on board

indicators.note: taking off the first letter removes the opening character of the word
travelling things move about, so these letters are mixed up
to overtake is read here as taking over, the outer letters wrapping the rest

blocks.note: taken as written before its first letter goes
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A jumbo jet takes off first, passing a plane with a husband aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo jet' reads as one aircraft, but the clue splits there: Jumbo is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo was a famous circus elephant, and the name is now a common nickname for any elephant.

clue.text: Second eleven shows spirit

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
an eleven is a cricket or football side

explanation.surface: The reserve team plays with real fighting spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second eleven' reads as a reserve side, but the second is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is used for energy and vigour, as in running out of steam, close to drive or spirit.

clue.text: Carry On Up The Khyber re-release ultimately must accept cut

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only each word's final letter counts
accepting something means taking it in, so the next word goes inside

blocks.note: the last letters of the four words
to sever is to cut

explanation.surface: A re-release of the Carry On Up the Khyber film has to be trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: Carry On Up the Khyber is a 1968 British comedy film; the definition is the first two words, the title's end is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on with something despite difficulty is to persevere, both meaning persisting steadily.

clue.text: Bore ought to finish off the wine

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its last letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: should means ought to
the final letter of the
red is a wine

explanation.surface: A tedious guest should really polish off the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a dull person, but it is the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden is to bear it, so shouldered is the past tense matching bore.

clue.text: Church on sex and desire

blocks.note: it is a coy word for sex
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: The church's views on sex and longing.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'Church on sex' puts church after sex.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving for something, as in an itch to travel.

clue.text: To do with fine dining, wanting starter to be huge

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, and the starter is the opening letter, so that letter goes

blocks.note: gastronomic means relating to good food

explanation.surface: A fancy restaurant meal without a first course that still turns out enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' sounds like a first course in the dining picture, but it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomic, like astronomical, describes something vast in scale, such as distances in space.

clue.text: Court studies motion before new award for loser

blocks.note: to court someone is to woo them
dens are private studies
a bowel motion
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A court considers a motion before a new prize for the defeated side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' and 'motion' suggest legal proceedings; motion is a bowel movement here.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden spoon is a joke booby prize given in Britain to whoever finishes last in a competition.

clue.text: Public holding River Exe back, work too hard

indicators.note: going back means the letters run in the opposite direction
holding something means having it inside, so the river goes within

blocks.note: overt means open, public
R for river plus Exe, a river in Devon

explanation.surface: Public authorities holding back a flooding river while overworking.
explanation.definitionFit: To overexert oneself is to push the body or mind beyond reasonable limits through excess effort.

clue.text: Friends turned up – in a hasty, careless way

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: pals are friends
the punctuation mark itself is a dash

explanation.surface: Friends arrived in a careless rush.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed dash looks like punctuation but supplies its own name as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash describes work done quickly and without care; as an adverb it means carelessly and hurriedly.

clue.text: See 2
Reform elected assuming one right-winger mostly means to reveal truth

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so one more letter is taken in
to reform is to form again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means not all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: Reform UK, elected with a right-winger in tow, mostly means truth will out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform' suggests the British party Reform UK, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie detector, or polygraph, is a machine designed to expose whether someone is telling the truth.

clue.text: See 7
Taking seconds to spend all his Euros – oddly getting tool

indicators.note: the seconds are the letters in second place in each word
oddly means the letters in odd positions, first, third and fifth

blocks.note: the second letter of each of the three words
the first, third and fifth letters of Euros

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker taking a few seconds to blow all the euros on a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The two selections split the clue: second letters come from the three words before Euros, and Euros itself gives its odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliers are a hand tool with pincer jaws for gripping, bending and cutting wire.

clue.text: Approach hospital following stroke

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the hospital letter goes at the end

blocks.note: to pat is to stroke gently
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A medical approach to treating stroke patients in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' suggests a medical emergency beside hospital, but it is a gentle touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a way leading to a place, and figuratively a course of action or method of approach.

clue.text: Busy wine bar admitting fifty students destroyed partition

indicators.note: a busy place is all hustle and movement, so these letters are jumbled
admitting means letting in, so further letters join inside

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for fifty
L is a learner, as on a British learner-driver plate; two of them for the plural

explanation.surface: A crowded wine bar lets in fifty students and the screen dividing the room gets smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berlin Wall divided East and West Berlin until it was torn down in 1989, a partition that was destroyed.

clue.text: Loose-limbed and ‘drunk’ on helium

blocks.note: lit is slang for drunk
He is the chemical symbol for helium

explanation.surface: Someone floppy and tipsy after inhaling helium at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' in quotes looks like an anagram signal, but it means LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means supple and flexible in body, which describes someone whose limbs move loosely.

clue.text: Climbing volcano – produces stake

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means going upwards, so the word is read from the bottom

blocks.note: Etna is a volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: Climbers on a volcano put their lives at stake.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is the sum each poker player puts in before the deal, a stake in the game.

clue.text: Trouble before navy crew start on the decking

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: ado means fuss or trouble
the Royal Navy
a crew is made up of men
the first letter of the

explanation.surface: Trouble breaks out before the naval crew start work on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decking' suggests a ship's deck, but it is the act of decorating.
explanation.definitionFit: Decking can mean decoration, as in decking the halls, and an adornment is an ornament or embellishment.

clue.text: Lime tree’s length

indicators.note: the apostrophe s stands for has, so the words hold the answer within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Measuring how tall a lime tree is.
explanation.definitionFit: A metre is the basic unit of length in the metric system, about 39 inches.

clue.text: Most insensitive firm is in Paris

blocks.note: hard means firm
est is French for is

explanation.surface: The most unfeeling company is based in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' suggests a company, but it means solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard can describe someone unfeeling or callous, so the superlative means the least sensitive of all.

clue.text: Calls for more space with 20 cycling

indicators.note: cycling goes round in a loop, so the opening letter moves to the end

blocks.note: an en is a printer's space
a score is twenty

explanation.surface: A space mission with twenty cyclists draws shouts for more.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 looks like a reference to 20-down, but it is simply the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Encores are the shouts from an audience asking a performer to come back and play again.
